text.p: The head of German reinsurer Munich Re said on Tuesday that the planned merger of Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechselbank and Bayerische Vereinsbank was "a very good and sensible solution".

Hans-Juergen Schinzler, management board chairman of Muenchner Rueckversicherung AG (Munich Re) said both it and "sister group" Allianz AG Holding would need to reorganise product distribution through the banks, as there was a lot of overlap.
Primary insurance group Ergo, in which Munich Re has a majority stake, is the result of the merger of German insurers Victoria and Hamburg-Mannheimer.
Regarding how the mega-merger would affect distribution and marketing, Schinzler said that at the moment, Vereinsbank distributed products for both Allianz and Hamburger-Mannheimer.
"Theoretically it is possible to imagine that the future Bayernbank will sell exclusively Allianz products, with Dresdner selling only Victoria and Ergo products," Schinzler said.

Schinzler told Handelsblatt newspaper that Ergo would aim to expand rapidly in the European market as a whole, and said that the formation of Ergo was Munich Re's last big expansionary move in the primary insurance market.

It was open to question whether the shareholding structure would remain in its current form, Schinzler said. He said he did not know what Allianz planned to do with its Ergo stake, whether the insurer would hold onto it, sell it on the stock exchange or sell it to Munich Re.
Cartel regulation would also have a role to play.
Schinzler insisted that the formation of Ergo did not pose a problem for Allianz AG Holding.
Through a 25 percent cross holding in Ergo held jointly by Munich Re and Allianz AG Holding, Allianz would retain 10 percent of Ergo. Munich Re is majority owner of Ergo, Schinzler said.
In a separate interview in the Tuesday edition of Die Welt newspaper, Schinzler said that Ergo did not necessarily plan to embark on a major European shopping tour and that it had other priorities.
"Ergo has to grow into a group and the synergy potential has to be realised. The integration will be hard work and will take Ergo years," Schinzler said.
Floods in the Oder region would also have an effect on Munich Re's business, Schinzler said, as it bore nearly all the burden of the cover for the damage along with Allianz.
"In insurance terms I don't see the sitation as dramatic. In terms of claims, such a huge event is not unusual," said Schinzler.
